domain.name: Cybersecurity & IT Operations
domain.description: Defensive identity, endpoint, patch, backup, network, monitoring, incident, and secrets practices.

competencies.name: Identity & Access Management
competencies.description: Control who can access systems and what they can do.
competencies.purpose: Control who can access systems and what they can do.

units.title: Identity & Access Management: core principle
units.content: Least privilege and separate administrator access reduce the damage from mistakes or account compromise.

units.title: Identity & Access Management: working procedure
units.content: Inventory accounts; assign owners/roles; remove stale access; separate admin from daily use; enable MFA where supported; review shared credentials; document exceptions.

units.title: Identity & Access Management: common failures
units.content: Avoid shared admin accounts, dormant access, permanent elevation for convenience, and permissions with no owner.

drills.title: Practice Identity & Access Management
drills.prompt: Design an access review and offboarding plan for staff, contractors, shared tools, and admin accounts.

competencies.name: Endpoint Security Hygiene
competencies.description: Keep laptops and workstations patched, recoverable, and resistant to common compromise.
competencies.purpose: Keep laptops and workstations patched, recoverable, and resistant to common compromise.

units.title: Endpoint Security Hygiene: core principle
units.content: Reduce attack surface before adding more security tools.

units.title: Endpoint Security Hygiene: working procedure
units.content: Enable supported updates; use malware protection; screen lock; storage encryption where practical; remove unused software; restrict admin rights; maintain backups.

units.title: Endpoint Security Hygiene: common failures
units.content: Avoid indefinite disabled updates, daily admin use, unknown extensions, pirated installers, and unsupported critical operating systems.

drills.title: Practice Endpoint Security Hygiene
drills.prompt: Create a security baseline for a Windows editing/development laptop used for client work.

competencies.name: Patching & Vulnerability Management
competencies.description: Track and remediate known weaknesses according to risk.
competencies.purpose: Track and remediate known weaknesses according to risk.

units.title: Patching & Vulnerability Management: core principle
units.content: Prioritize exposure, exploitability, asset criticality, and available mitigations rather than raw vulnerability count.

units.title: Patching & Vulnerability Management: working procedure
units.content: Inventory software/assets; monitor vendor notices; classify exposure; test critical updates when feasible; deploy; verify service health; document deferrals and compensating controls.

units.title: Patching & Vulnerability Management: common failures
units.content: Avoid blind production patching with no rollback, ignoring firmware/dependencies, and postponing critical exposed fixes indefinitely.

drills.title: Practice Patching & Vulnerability Management
drills.prompt: Prioritize updates across an exposed server, workstation, router, plugin, and dev library.

competencies.name: Backup & Recovery
competencies.description: Design backups that can actually restore business data after failure or corruption.
competencies.purpose: Design backups that can actually restore business data after failure or corruption.

units.title: Backup & Recovery: core principle
units.content: A backup is only proven when restoration works.

units.title: Backup & Recovery: working procedure
units.content: Identify critical data; keep multiple copies on different media/systems; protect at least one copy from ordinary compromise; define retention; test restores; record recovery objectives.

units.title: Backup & Recovery: common failures
units.content: Avoid sync as the only backup, one always-connected drive, no retention, and backups whose credentials exist only on the protected machine.

drills.title: Practice Backup & Recovery
drills.prompt: Design backup and restore for client footage, project files, exports, and business documents.

competencies.name: Network Troubleshooting
competencies.description: Diagnose connectivity problems methodically from local device through service.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose connectivity problems methodically from local device through service.

units.title: Network Troubleshooting: core principle
units.content: Isolate the failing layer before changing configuration.

units.title: Network Troubleshooting: working procedure
units.content: Check link; IP/gateway/DNS; local gateway; external IP reachability; DNS resolution; target service/port; compare another device; record each change.

units.title: Network Troubleshooting: common failures
units.content: Avoid resetting everything first, changing multiple layers together, assuming Wi-Fi bars prove internet access, or ignoring VPN/proxy state.

drills.title: Practice Network Troubleshooting
drills.prompt: Diagnose a laptop that reaches the router but cannot browse while another device works.

competencies.name: Logging & Monitoring
competencies.description: Collect enough operational and security signals to detect and investigate failures.
competencies.purpose: Collect enough operational and security signals to detect and investigate failures.

units.title: Logging & Monitoring: core principle
units.content: Useful monitoring is actionable, attributable, and retained long enough to investigate normal incidents.

units.title: Logging & Monitoring: working procedure
units.content: Identify critical services; choose health/error signals; preserve logs; set actionable alerts; test alert delivery; review noise; protect sensitive data in logs.

units.title: Logging & Monitoring: common failures
units.content: Avoid alerts on every minor event, unsynchronized clocks, secrets in logs, and dashboards with no response owner.

drills.title: Practice Logging & Monitoring
drills.prompt: Define health checks and alerts for FREEOS API, database, Ollama, and disk space.

competencies.name: Security Incident Response
competencies.description: Contain, preserve evidence, recover, and learn from suspected security events.
competencies.purpose: Contain, preserve evidence, recover, and learn from suspected security events.

units.title: Security Incident Response: core principle
units.content: Containment matters, but wiping or deleting evidence too early can hide scope and cause.

units.title: Security Incident Response: working procedure
units.content: Identify event; assess impact; isolate affected systems when warranted; preserve logs; reset credentials from trusted systems; eradicate cause; restore; monitor; document lessons.

units.title: Security Incident Response: common failures
units.content: Avoid deleting logs, reusing compromised credentials, reconnecting before root cause is addressed, or declaring certainty without evidence.

drills.title: Practice Security Incident Response
drills.prompt: Plan first actions after unusual login alerts and unauthorized messages from a business account.

competencies.name: Secrets & Secure Configuration
competencies.description: Protect passwords, tokens, API keys, and sensitive configuration from accidental exposure.
competencies.purpose: Protect passwords, tokens, API keys, and sensitive configuration from accidental exposure.

units.title: Secrets & Secure Configuration: core principle
units.content: Reusable credentials should not live in source code, screenshots, logs, or ordinary chat.

units.title: Secrets & Secure Configuration: working procedure
units.content: Inventory secrets; remove plaintext from code/docs; use protected configuration; restrict permissions; separate dev/test/prod; rotate exposed values; document recovery.

units.title: Secrets & Secure Configuration: common failures
units.content: Avoid committed .env files, shared personal passwords, debug logs with tokens, and recovery codes stored beside the primary credential.

drills.title: Practice Secrets & Secure Configuration
drills.prompt: Create a repository checklist for preventing secret leakage through source, logs, screenshots, and backups.
